Meld the rest of the implicit heaps

The weak, min-max and interval heaps meld by appending and rebuilding
bottom-up, the beap by repeated insertion, and the sorted array by a
merge of two runs. All of it is proved at --level=4.

The min-max and interval sifts had to be relativized to be callable on a
node whose ancestors are not yet in order: they now take the lowest index
whose subtree claims are in force, and a build walks that bound down from
one past the last node. The interval heap needs two such bounds, because
a build places the low end of a node while its high end is still
unplaced.

Heaps.Models gains a range model, Occurrences_In, with the lemmas tying
it to the prefix model, peeling a range at its low end and splitting two
ranges back into a prefix. The sorted array's merge runs backwards so
that the array only ever holds two live regions, which is what the prefix
model can be recovered from -- and it is the faster direction anyway.
EOF
